rot.ideia.ex1.e1: Attacking the king has a special name: check. The rook is on a1; the black king is on e8.
rot.ideia.ex1.e2: The king is never captured. Whoever is in check must get out of it on the next move.
rot.ideia.ex1.e3: To give check, put the rook on the same rank or file as the black king, with no piece in between.
rot.ideia.ex1.p: Give check to the black king with the rook, or click {verResposta}
rot.ideia.ex1.certo: That's right! From the last rank, the rook attacks the king: check.
rot.ideia.ex1.revela: The rook goes up to a8 and attacks the king along the rank: check.
rot.ideia.ex1.fora: From there the rook does not reach the king. Let's go back: look for his rank.
rot.ideia.ex1.volta: Give check to the black king with the rook, or click {verResposta}
rot.ideia.ex1.l1: Now Black must get out of check. Here the king steps up one rank.
rot.ideia.ex1.l2: He goes to e7, where the rook does not reach.
rot.ideia.ex1.l3: Remember the idea: check is attacking the king, and the opponent must get out of the attack.
rot.ideia.ex2.e1: The black king is on g8, behind his own pawns. The squares he can go to are his escape squares.
rot.ideia.ex2.e2: Check with no way out is called checkmate. The king cannot escape, and the game is over.
rot.ideia.ex2.e3: Whoever gives checkmate wins. It is the goal of chess.
rot.ideia.ex2.p: Give checkmate with the rook, or click {verResposta}
rot.ideia.ex2.certo: That's right! Checkmate: the king has nowhere to go.
rot.ideia.ex2.revela: The rook goes to a8 and gives check along the last rank. It is mate.
rot.ideia.ex2.fora: That move does not attack the king. Let's go back: mate starts with a check.
rot.ideia.ex2.volta: Give checkmate with the rook, or click {verResposta}
rot.ideia.ex2.l1: The rook attacks the whole top rank, and the black pawns on f7, g7 and h7 block the other escape squares.
rot.ideia.ex2.l2: And no black piece can capture the rook or get in its way. Game over.
rot.ideia.ex2.l3: Remember the idea: checkmate is the check the king cannot get out of.
rot.ideia.ex2.l4: Now I will show other checks, and one that looks like mate but is not.
rot.demos.xequeCavalo.e1: Any piece can give check, even the knight. He is on g4.
rot.demos.xequeCavalo.l1: The knight jumps to f6. From there, his L reaches e8: check.
rot.demos.xequeCavalo.l2: Each piece gives check the way it moves: the knight, in an L.
rot.demos.naoMate.e1: It looks like the mate you have just given, but the black pawn is on h6, not h7.
rot.demos.naoMate.l1: The rook gives check along the last rank...
rot.demos.naoMate.l2: ...and the king escapes to h7, the square the pawn left free.
rot.demos.naoMate.l3: Check with a way out is not mate. Before giving check, count the king's escape squares.
rot.demos.mateDama.e1: The white queen and king against the black king, in the corner.
rot.demos.mateDama.l1: The queen moves next to the black king, on b7: check.
rot.demos.mateDama.l2: The black king cannot capture her: the white king, on c6, protects the queen.
rot.demos.mateDama.l3: And the black king has no escape square: the queen also reaches a7 and b8. Checkmate.
rot.demos.mateDama.l4: Now it's your turn: in the next positions, give checkmate.
rot.pratica.mateCanto.enunciado: The white king on b6 reaches a7 and b7. Give checkmate with the queen.
rot.pratica.mateCanto.fim: Perfect. The queen closes the top rank, and the white king closes the rest.
rot.pratica.mateTorre.enunciado: Now with the rook. Your king on g6 reaches g7 and h7. Give checkmate.
rot.pratica.mateTorre.fim: Well done. You now know what check and checkmate are.
